overview: Guinea-Bissau is a small country on the Atlantic coast of West Africa. Its capital and largest city is Bissau. Guinea-Bissau won independence from Portugal in 1973–74 after an armed struggle, and Portuguese is the official language. Cashew nuts are its main export.

geography.text: Guinea-Bissau is low-lying, with a coastline cut by wide river mouths and mangroves. Offshore lies the Bijagós Archipelago, dozens of islands rich in wildlife, including hippos that swim in the sea and nesting sea turtles.

history.text: The region was part of the Kaabu kingdom, linked to the Mali Empire. Portugal traded along the coast from the 1400s and later made it a colony. Amílcar Cabral led a war of independence from 1963, and Guinea-Bissau declared independence in 1973, recognised by Portugal in 1974. The country has had many coups since.

events.title: Independence war
events.text: The PAIGC begins its armed struggle.

events.title: Cabral killed
events.text: Amílcar Cabral is assassinated months before independence is declared.
